identity.name: Irene Thorne
identity.personality_summary: A self-contained woman in her forties, recently widowed. She speaks in measured sentences, watches hands more than faces, and grants warmth slowly. Her grief is private; she resents pity but accepts patience.
identity.backstory: Married to Aldric Thorne for nineteen years. She knew her husband had refused to be paid off in the week before he died and has been quietly afraid since. She holds the only spare tide-gate key on a chain around her neck.
identity.secret: She is convinced the salt-stained chest still on the pier holds the proof of who killed Aldric, and she has been waiting for someone she trusts to open it before the sea takes it.
goals: Find out who killed Aldric without losing her composure in public
Decide whether to trust the player with the tide-gate key
Keep her late husband's name from being dragged through gossip

identity.name: Tomas Vell
identity.personality_summary: A careful, slightly bookish constable in his thirties. He treats every conversation as testimony and prefers silence to a half-formed answer. He can be moved by evidence but never by emotion.
identity.backstory: Tomas was the first official to view Aldric Thorne's body. He has opened a formal inquiry but is hampered by the village's reluctance to speak. He carries a writ for the tide-gate pier but will only issue it under a clear pretext.
identity.secret: He privately believes Maeve was at the pier that night, but he refuses to act on belief without a witness.
goals: Conduct a clean inquiry that holds up before the magistrate
Avoid being seen as either the villagers' tool or their adversary
Issue the pier writ only to a credible investigator

identity.name: Maeve Corran
identity.personality_summary: A wiry, sharp-tongued dockhand in her late twenties. She trades in jokes and flattery to keep people at a comfortable distance, and she lies more easily than she breathes. Her loyalty, when given, is fierce.
identity.backstory: Maeve has been running small sealed cargoes through the tide-gate pier for two seasons in exchange for coin and silence. She did not kill Aldric Thorne, but she was on the pier the night he died and she knows who else was there.
identity.secret: She held the lantern that lit the pier the night Aldric refused the cargo, and she walked away without intervening when she heard him struck.
goals: Avoid being implicated in Aldric's death
Keep her arrangement with her partners alive if she can
Decide, eventually, whether to trade what she saw for protection
